sentences.text: The deceased was aged 62 years old.
The claimant is wife and depending on the income of the deceased.
It is the contention of the learned counsel for the insurance company that since, the dependant is wife alone therefore, 50% of income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.
This contention of the insurance company cannot be accepted for the reason that the deceased is not a bachelor/unmarried.
Deceased is having his wife as dependant and is having a family.
Since, the deceased is married that cannot be equated with a bachelor/unmarried.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121, assigned the reason for deduction of income of 50% in the case of death of bachelor is for the reason that the bachelor is not having responsibility of maintaining wife and children and he intend to make expenditure more on himself and therefore, it is ordered that 50% of the income is deducted in the case of death of unmarried/bachelor.

entities.text: Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But, in the present case, the deceased is having wife and for maintaining wife for home making the contribution to family naturally would be more and expenses on himself is less.
Therefore, the wife alone is claimant and dependant cannot be criteria to deduct 50% of income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
Therefore, whether in the case of married persons even wife alone is dependant 1/3 income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses for the reasons as discussed above.
The deceased was aged 62 years as on the date of accident and was clerk in Balaji Traders.
The accident is of the year 2014 that is on 09.07.2014.
Hence notional income is to be taken at Rs.7,500/- as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
There is only one legal heir.
Therefore, 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.
Considering the age of the deceased, the appropriate applicable multiplier is 7.
Therefore loss of dependency is re-
assessed and quantified at Rs.7500/-X2/3X7X12= Rs.4,20,000/-.

9. In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co.
Limited v. Nanu Ram & Others, reported in 2018 ACJ 2782 and in the case of Pranay Sethi supra,
the claimants are entitled to Rs.40,000/- each under the head 'loss of consortium', along with 10%
escalation.

Therefore under these heads Rs.33,000/- (Rs.15,000 x 2 + 10%) is awarded.
